name: What should I do if my renovation uncovers old wiring or plumbing?

mainEntity.name: During a living-space renovation, what happens if the contractor finds outdated wiring, knob-and-tube, or bad plumbing behind the walls?
mainEntity.text: During a living-space renovation, what happens if the contractor finds outdated wiring, knob-and-tube, or bad plumbing behind the walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes often reveal surprises once walls or floors are opened. Outdated wiring, damaged plumbing, termite issues, or nonstandard framing can force the project to pause while the problem is assessed. The contractor should explain what was found, whether the issue affects safety or code compliance, and whether the fix must happen before finishing work can resume. Homeowners should expect some level of contingency in any renovation budget because hidden conditions are common and can be expensive. The best way to reduce stress is to ask your contractor how they handle discoveries, who approves changes, and how pricing is documented. If the issue is significant, the scope may need reengineering or a permit revision. Clear communication matters because delays often happen when the homeowner wants the original plan but the hidden condition makes that plan unsafe or impractical.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden electrical or plumbing problems usually require a change order, revised scope, and possibly new permits before work can continue. The contractor should stop affected work, document the issue, and give you repair options with updated pricing. Unexpected conditions are common in older homes and should be budgeted for upfront.
